sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints: winter, mountain, rural and work-zone driving; defensive driving basics

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
The two skid instructions differ by brakes: with anti-lock brakes you ease off the gas and push on the brake while steering, without them you use threshold braking just short of lockup. [A01]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty three; confusable sec11-F08 vs sec11-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
A generic skid starts with both feet off the pedals, while an anti-lock skid adds pushing on the brake; in both, steer where you want to go. [A01]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty three; confusable sec11-F03 vs sec11-F08. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Four-wheel drive adds traction but not stopping power; it cannot stop any sooner than an ordinary car. [A01]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty two; prereq sec11-F05. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
Bridges, overpasses and shaded spots can stay icy when the surrounding pavement is not, so a clear road can still hold icy patches. [A01]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty two; prereq sec11-F02. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
On a mountain grade the uphill driver has the right-of-way, and a slow uphill vehicle should keep right or pull off to let others by. [A01]
Why it matters: group mountain driving; difficulty two; prereq sec11-F17. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
Hand-held phone use has a hands-free exception, but texting does not; both allow contacting police or fire and emergencies. [A02]
Why it matters: group distraction law; difficulty three; confusable sec11-F32 vs sec11-F33. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A02
Three different times guide your eyes and spacing: look 10 seconds ahead, check the mirror every 5 to 8 seconds, and leave three seconds behind the car ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: group scanning; difficulty three; confusable sec11-F36 vs sec11-F37 vs sec11-F38. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
Work-zone and school-zone fines are both doubled, and most work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty two; prereq sec11-F28 and sec11-F29. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0021]

Misconception: chains and snow tires make slick pavement safe; they can still slip. [A01]
Misconception: you only need to scrape a small hole in the frost for a short trip; clear all ice, snow and frost. [A01]
Misconception: the required bicyclist passing gap is enough on rural roads; slower speeds and more room are advised. [A01]
Misconception: following the rules guarantees others will too; drive defensively and ignore aggressive drivers. [A02]
Mnemonic: Left, right, left before you enter. [A02]
Mnemonic: Feet off, eyes and wheels where you want to go. [A01]
Glossary: Threshold braking means pressing the brake just short of locking the wheels. [A01]
Glossary: Washboarding means a series of potholes, often on gravel roads, that can upset steering and control. [A01]
Glossary: Defensive driving means driving to protect yourself and others from unsafe or unexpected situations. [A02]
Glossary: Push-pull-slide means one of the two preferred ways to turn the wheel, the other being hand-over-hand. [A02]
